name: CharXiv
intro: 图表理解在多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）应用于分析科学论文或财务报告等实际任务中扮演着关键角色。现有数据集常侧重于过度简化和同质化的图表，导致对模型进展的评估过于乐观。CharXiv是一个全面的评估套件，包含2,323个来自arXiv论文的自然、具有挑战性和多样化的图表。它包括描述性问题和推理问题，所有图表和问题均由人类专家精心挑选、整理和验证。
org: Princeton Language and Intelligence (PLI), Princeton University, University of Wisconsin, Madison, T
build_method: arXiv科学图表筛选, 研究生人工标注, 专家核验
metric: GPT-4o裁判准确率（人工参考答案）
task_type: 开放式描述问答, 图表推理问答
eval_feature: 描述与推理双任务, 每图3道可回答描述题+1道不可回答题+1道推理题, 人类基线
build_method_en: arXiv Scientific-chart Filtering, Graduate-student Annotation, Expert Verification
eval_feature_en: Descriptive and Reasoning Tracks, Three Answerable plus One Unanswerable Descriptive Question per Chart, One Reasoning Question per Chart, Human Baseline
intro_en: Chart understanding plays a crucial role in applying multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to real-world tasks such as analyzing scientific papers or financial reports. Existing datasets often focus on overly simplified and homogeneous charts, leading to overly optimistic assessments of model progress. CharXiv is a comprehensive evaluation suite containing 2,323 natural, challenging, and diverse charts sourced from arXiv papers. It includes both descriptive and reasoning questions, with all charts and questions carefully selected, curated, and validated by human experts.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2406.18521 and the NeurIPS 2024 paper, dataset-construction and evaluation sections. The authors download arXiv preprints from eight academic subjects from January 2020 through September 2023, extract and re-render figures, then apply SigLIP chart prefiltering, graduate-student selection for visual diversity, pairwise-similarity deduplication, and removal of blurry or unclearly labeled charts. The 2,323 retained charts split into 1,000 validation and 1,323 test charts. Each chart receives four descriptive questions selected from 19 templates across information extraction, enumeration, pattern recognition, counting, and compositionality; three are answerable and one is intentionally unanswerable, totaling 9,292. Each chart also receives one manually written, definite-answer reasoning question, totaling 2,323. Human experts verify charts, questions, and answers. Zero-shot responses are graded by GPT-4o against human references; a 400-item audit reports 98.5-percent agreement with human grading. Human baselines under the same instructions are 80.5 percent for reasoning and 92.1 percent for descriptive questions.
